Q28: the answer is not an answer. The eval is kept in a dedicated eval folder under the plan folder (the plan's evals sit under the plan, not a separate folder). Mark in CLAUDE.md that any builder agent or skill that builds the software does not read this folder. Q29: the eval tests the ICE of the slice's features and their capabilities: every intent and expectation is met, and no failure condition breaks. It is a product test; it does not know how it is built (browser, mobile app, CLI, backend). Its first step is to find how it was built. It asks for a guide to how the system is used; the build delivers that guide; the eval uses it to test. Rest are fine.

No, eval is testing the work item against the piece, and all of the ICE sits in the work items, the epics and stories. The eval should understand what the epic is delivering, and test that against the product. All the information about ICE sits in the story itself. I don't want two or three different things to talk to ICE and have different interpretations. The slice play does all the interpretation, builds the epic and stories, and that's what the eval should read.

Shape slice should just shape the slice and leave it as is, and transition automatically to building the plan, which should then create the epic. I don't want to duplicate the functionality. Shape slice stops at shaping the slice, with an automatic continuation to building the plan. The third thing it automatically goes to is building the eval. Three things happen: 1. shaping the slice, 2. building the plan, which gets everything ready, 3. building the eval. These are three plays, and together they become the shaping loop.
